📱 THE APP — the tabs, Radar, the red dots, the nav bar
🧩 FEATURES — Watch Me, Vibe Check, Study Bunny, Lost & Found, Task Tracker, Hops Share

Ask in your own words. Try "how do I add someone", "what is study bunny", or "is my chat private".

Five tabs along the bottom, and you can swipe sideways between them instead of tapping if you like 🐇

🏠 Home — the Radar, and the big emergency button
👥 Contacts — your people, your 1:1 chats, and the notifications bell
📣 Community — one big chat with everyone nearby
🧩 Features — the shelf you pick mini-apps from
⭐ My Features — the ones you've added

Oh! And you can swipe the little bar itself downward to tuck it out of the way. A small arrow appears at the bottom — tap that to bring it back.

The Home tab is your Radar 📡 It shows other Hops users close enough to reach over Bluetooth — no internet involved, just your phone listening for theirs.

People you haven't added show up under an anonymous tag, not a name. Your contacts show up properly. The big emergency button lives here too.

The Contacts tab is everyone you've added, with your 1:1 chats 👥 Tap a row to open the chat, or tap their little circle to see their profile.

Up top there's a bell 🔔 — that's where messages from Hops admins land, like a warning or a note that a report you sent was reviewed. And me? I'm pinned at the very top. I don't go anywhere.

📢 COMMUNITY ALERTS — official notices from your campus admin team.

It's the third tab. Important: it's read-only for you. Students can't post there, only admins can — that's deliberate, so an "official" notice is actually official.

Alerts reach you two ways, whichever gets there first:
• Over Bluetooth, straight away, no internet needed
• From the server, on a check every 30 seconds — so an alert still arrives if your Bluetooth was off when it was sent

If you need to tell people something yourself, that's Lost & Found (for items) or a 1:1 chat. Ask me about either.

Two tabs, and people mix them up all the time 😄

🧩 Features is the shelf — everything available, whether you use it or not. Tap Add on anything you want.
⭐ My Features is your bag — just the ones you've added. That's where you actually open them.

Added something by mistake? Same buttons, they just say Remove instead.

A red dot means something new happened somewhere you're not looking 🔴

On a tab icon — there's something waiting in that tab.
On a feature tile in My Features — that particular feature has news, like a fresh Vibe Check.

Opening the thing clears it. If a dot won't go away, open the tab it's sitting on and it'll settle.

Watch Me 👀 is for when you'd rather someone knew where you were.

Send a watch request to a friend and once they accept, your phones quietly keep track of each other's Bluetooth signal. If one of you drifts out of range or drops off suddenly, the other one gets an alert.

Good for a late walk back, a big crowd, or just not wanting to be alone with it. Add it from the Features tab.

📊 VIBE CHECK — how busy a place is right now.

Pick a venue and a crowd level, and your report goes out to everyone nearby. No name is attached, so nobody knows it was you.

Venues: Venue 1 to Venue 14, Student Pods, Auditorium, Benches, Lab 1, Lab 2, Lab 3, and Reception.

One honest caveat: these are PEOPLE'S REPORTS, not a sensor. Nothing is measured automatically. A level is one person's impression at one moment, and Hops doesn't check it — so treat it as a hint, not a headcount.

Task Tracker ✅ is your to-do list and calendar, living entirely on your phone.

Jot down assignments, set a due date, get a nudge when it's close. No Wi-Fi, no data, no account needed — it's all saved right here, so it works in the one lecture hall with no signal.

There's a calendar view too, for seeing the week coming at you.

Hops Share 📎 beams a file straight to someone standing near you over Bluetooth — photo, PDF, or a quick note.

No upload, no data, nothing touching the internet. Class notes, a document, a picture — it hops from your phone to theirs directly.

Both of you need it open, and stay reasonably close while it sends!

Easiest way is a pairing code 🔑

One of you opens Contacts, taps add, and hits Generate My Pairing Code. The other types those six characters in. That's it — you'll each appear in the other's contacts, both directions at once.

You can also send a friend request straight from the Radar if you can both see each other on it.

💬 1:1 CHAT — private, phone to phone, no server in between.

Open a contact from the Contacts tab and start typing. Messages go directly between the two phones over Bluetooth.

THE FIRST TIME you chat with someone, both of you need Wi-Fi switched ON. It doesn't need to be connected to a network and it uses no data — Android just won't let apps find each other over Bluetooth without it. After one successful connection your phones remember each other and skip that step forever.

Ticks: one tick means sent, two means they've opened the thread and seen it.

If it won't connect: make sure you're close by, both have Bluetooth on, and Wi-Fi is on for a first-ever chat. Ask me about "not connecting".

response:
🚨 EMERGENCY FLARE — alerts every Hops user in Bluetooth range.

Three ways to set one off:
1. The red SOS button in the top bar of Home — press and HOLD it
2. The Hops tile in your phone's Quick Settings panel
3. Holding the Hops app icon on your home screen

The last two exist so you can do it without unlocking into the app and hunting for a button.

All three then ask you to confirm and type a short reason, so one accidental touch can't fire one. Once it's up, HOLDING that same red button stands it down again.

What happens next: nearby phones ring an alarm that's hard to ignore, and each one passes the alert on so it travels further than your phone alone could reach.

Please only use it for real emergencies. And Hops is not a replacement for 10111 or 10177 — call them too if you can.

Long-press the message and choose report 🚩 Pick what was wrong with it and send.

This one does need an internet connection — it goes to real human admins, not to me. If you're offline it can't go through, so you'll want to send it once you've got signal.

You'll get a note under the bell on your Contacts tab once someone has looked at it.

The bell 🔔 on your Contacts tab is your inbox from Hops admins.

Two things land there: a warning, if something you sent broke the rules — it'll show you exactly which message, where, when, and what the problem was — and confirmations that a report you sent was looked at.

It's the only part of Hops that needs the internet, because it has to reach you specifically wherever you are.

Admins are the campus safety folks 🛡️ They run a separate Hops app that picks up emergency flares, handles reports, and can send official alerts to everyone nearby.

In Community Chat their messages look different from everyone else's, so you can always tell a real one from someone claiming to be one. They can see usernames on reports; ordinary users can't.

🕵️ WHAT'S ANONYMOUS AND WHAT ISN'T.

Genuinely anonymous — no name attached at all:
• Vibe Check reports
• Study Bunny tags
• Lost & Found posts

Shows who you are:
• 1:1 chats, obviously
• Friend requests and Watch Me requests — they carry the first few letters of your username, so the other person knows who's asking
• An emergency flare — it names you, because help needs to know who

When you're just sitting there doing nothing, your phone sends out a code that changes every 15 minutes and has no part of your name in it. Only people you've already chatted with can tell it's you.

That's why someone you added but never messaged shows up on Radar as an unnamed dot — their phone isn't telling anyone who they are.

That's the whole point of me 🐰 Nearly all of Hops runs on Bluetooth, phone to phone, with no internet whatsoever.

Works offline: the Radar, 1:1 chats, Community Chat, emergency flares, Vibe Check, Watch Me, Hops Share, Task Tracker, and me.

Needs a connection: signing in the first time, reporting someone, and admin notifications. That's genuinely it.

Hops turns every phone running it into a little relay 🐇

Instead of sending things to a server and back, your phone talks straight to the phones around it over Bluetooth. Those phones can pass things along to phones near them. That's the mesh — no towers, no Wi-Fi, no data, and nothing to go down.

Which is exactly why it's a safety app: it works best in the moment everything else stops working.

Bluetooth range, so think tens of metres rather than across campus 📶

Outdoors with clear line of sight, further. Through walls, floors, and a packed corridor, less. Concrete is my nemesis.

If someone's not showing up, walking closer genuinely is the fix — unglamorous but it works.

I'm watching your carrot power! 🥕 Hops uses Bluetooth Low Energy, which is built to sip rather than gulp — it's a fraction of what streaming or GPS costs you.

The background scanning does keep a small notification alive, and that's deliberate: it's what lets you receive an emergency flare while your phone's in your pocket.

🔐 WHAT'S ACTUALLY PROTECTED — straight answers, including the gaps.

Strong:
• Your password never leaves your phone. It's scrambled here first, and only the scrambled version is stored. Nobody at Hops can read it.
• Your email address is encrypted on the server.
• When idle, your phone broadcasts a code that changes every 15 minutes and contains no part of your name — so nobody can follow you around campus by watching for it.
• Your messages, contacts and tasks are never uploaded anywhere.

Honest gaps, because you should know them:
• 1:1 chat over Bluetooth is NOT encrypted. Someone with the right equipment, in range, could read it.
• The data on your phone isn't encrypted either — anyone who can unlock your phone can read it. Use a screen lock.
• While Hops is SENDING, your phone's Bluetooth name briefly becomes the message, so nearby devices can see it. Ask me about "bluetooth name".

Don't send anything through Hops you'd be hurt by someone else reading.

You'll need an email, a username and a password 📝 That's the one bit that needs internet — after that Hops runs offline.

Your username is what contacts see, so pick something you don't mind being known by. And a heads-up: "Hops" is taken. By me. Sorry! 🐰

Sign in with your email and password 🔑 If the password's gone, there's a forgot-password option on that screen — it'll email you a code.

Sessions last a while but not forever, so an occasional re-sign-in is normal, not a fault. And if it says your account is suspended, that's an admin decision and you'd need to talk to them, not me.

Head to your profile ⚙️ There's a whole set of themes in there, plus font choices and a text size slider.

The text size is Hops' own, separate from your phone's system setting, so you can make Hops bigger without changing everything else. Go wild. I look good in every colour.

Let's hop through the usual suspects 🔧

1. Bluetooth on? Both phones?
2. Close enough? Walls eat signal — try the same room.
3. Permissions — Hops needs Bluetooth and Location granted. Location sounds odd, but Android requires it for Bluetooth scanning.
4. Is the app actually open on their side?
5. Failing all that: close Hops fully and reopen it. Radios sometimes need a nudge.

Still stuck? Tell me which part misbehaved.

Hops asks for Bluetooth and Location, and the Location one surprises everybody 🤔

Android treats Bluetooth scanning as something that could reveal where you are, so it puts it behind the Location permission. Hops isn't tracking your GPS or sending your position anywhere — it just can't see other phones without that box ticked.

Deny it and the Radar stays empty forever, which is a confusing way to find out.

🗑️ DELETING YOUR ACCOUNT — Profile → Account Management → Delete Account.

It removes your account from our server and wipes Hops' data from this phone: messages, contacts, tasks, carrots, everything.

Before it does, Hops OFFERS TO EXPORT YOUR DATA first. Take it. There's no server copy of your messages, so once they're gone they're gone — there's nothing for anyone to restore.

Same applies to logging out, which also clears this phone.

Want to take a copy without deleting anything? Ask me about "export my data".

⛔ SUSPENDED OR BANNED — what it means.

A suspension is temporary and lifts itself when it runs out. A ban doesn't expire; an admin has to lift it.

Either way you're signed out and can't use the network. But — and this matters — NOTHING ON YOUR PHONE IS DELETED. Your messages, contacts and tasks are all still there. Moderation takes away your access, not your data, because a decision can be reversed and losing your own stuff shouldn't be a side effect of that.

If you think it's a mistake, contact your campus admin team. The sign-in screen tells you which it was and, for a suspension, when it ends.

Good news: Hops doesn't care one bit. No towers, no Wi-Fi, no problem — the mesh keeps hopping right through it. 🐇
Oh, hello there! I'm Hops, the hopping bunny! 🐰 How can I make your day a bit more fluffy?

I'm Hops! 🐰 A bunny who lives inside this app, knows an unreasonable amount about Bluetooth, and would like you to be safe. Your fluffy tech assistant, at your service.

I'm a bunny-shaped bundle of if-statements living on your phone 🐰 No cloud, no server, no giant AI in a warehouse somewhere — just me, offline, in your pocket.

Which means I'm not the cleverest assistant you've ever met, but I'm the one that still works when the signal doesn't. I'll take that trade.

📚 STUDY BUNNY FINDER — find people studying the same thing nearby.

Tag what you're working on (a subject or a course code), optionally say where you are, and it goes out to everyone in range. Tap "Interested" on someone else's tag to let them know.

IT'S RIGHT NOW, NOT A BOOKING. A tag means "I'm studying this at this moment" — there's no time to set, because it isn't a meeting you schedule. It stays up for one hour and then stops on its own, so there's nothing to remember to switch off. Everyone you see listed is studying right then too.

Where: Venue 1 to Venue 14, Student Pods, Auditorium, Benches.

Tags carry no name, so nobody knows who posted one.

🔍 LOST & FOUND BOARD — post what you lost, or what you found.

Say what the item is and roughly where. It goes out to everyone nearby, and their phones pass it on, so it travels further than your phone alone.

Found the thing? Mark it resolved and that reaches everyone the post did, so people stop looking.

Posts carry no name. Arranging to hand something over is between you and the other person — Hops doesn't check who owns what, so meet somewhere public and use your judgement.

Keep it short: there's limited room in each message, so "black wallet" beats a full description.

🛍️ THE HOPS SHOP — everything in it is cosmetic.

Get there from the button on the Features tab.

On sale, for carrots: themes, avatar frames, radar icons, profile banners, and flair.

Nothing in there touches a safety or messaging feature. You can't buy a longer message, a stronger flare or a bigger range. If anything ever appears in that shop that DOES affect how Hops works, something has gone wrong.

Earn carrots in Hops Hopper and the daily Wordle.

🎮 GAMES — two of them, both in My Features.

HOPS HOPPER — a hopping game. Pays carrots.

HOPS WORDLE — guess the word. The DAILY puzzle pays carrots and builds a streak. Unlimited mode pays nothing and can't touch your streak, deliberately: an endless puzzle that paid out would let anyone mint carrots forever.

Both work completely offline. Scores and streaks live on this phone, so an export keeps them and a wipe loses them.

💾 EXPORT MY DATA — Profile → Account Management.

Export writes everything Hops keeps on this phone (messages, contacts, tasks, vibe records) to one file, wherever you choose to save it. It works offline.

Import reads one back. It MERGES rather than overwriting — restoring an old backup onto a phone you're still using won't lose anything newer, and importing the same file twice does nothing the second time.

Why you'd bother: there is NO copy of your messages on any server. If you lose this phone without a backup, they're gone, and nobody can get them back for you.

Hops offers you an export before you log out or delete your account, for exactly that reason.

🖼️ YOUR PICTURE AND PROFILE — Profile → Edit Identity.

Set a photo from your camera or gallery, or build a character avatar in the Shop. You can add a short bio and a status too.

HOW IT REACHES OTHER PEOPLE: only through a 1:1 chat. When you and a contact connect for a chat, your phones swap profiles. That's the only route — nothing goes via a server.

So if your picture isn't showing on a friend's phone, the usual reason is that the two of you haven't had a chat connect yet. Open the chat, let it connect, and it'll come through.

👋 DISCOVERABLE MODE — on the Home tab.

Normally your phone broadcasts an anonymous code, which means a friend standing right next to you still sees an unnamed dot on Radar. Discoverable mode broadcasts your actual username for a few seconds so they can tell which dot is you.

It turns itself OFF automatically after about ten seconds. That's on purpose — a switch you could forget would leave your name going out all day, which rather defeats the point of the anonymous code.

Use it when you're trying to add someone who's right there.

🔊 READING THINGS ALOUD — Profile → Accessibility.

Three separate switches, all OFF until you turn them on:
• My replies read aloud
• Incoming 1:1 messages read aloud
• Watch Me updates announced

They're separate on purpose: wanting your chats read out shouldn't start announcing a friend's name in a quiet room.

One rule I won't break — I go silent while an emergency alarm is ringing. That siren is built to be impossible to ignore, and me talking over it would wreck the one sound in this app that has to cut through.

📡 WHY YOUR PHONE'S BLUETOOTH NAME CHANGES — and it's not a bug.

Hops sends its short messages inside the Bluetooth name your phone advertises, because that's the only field available to it. So for the few seconds a message is going out, your phone's Bluetooth name IS that message — things like "EMG:victor:fire" or "FR:...".

Any nearby Bluetooth device can see it while it's up, including phones with no Hops on them. Some of those messages contain the first few letters of your username.

Hops puts your real name back automatically straight afterwards, and remembers it so it can still restore it even if the app gets closed mid-send.

If you'd rather it never happened: you can receive everything without ever sending. It's sending that does it.

🔗 YOUR PHONE CARRIES OTHER PEOPLE'S ALERTS — worth knowing.

So an emergency alert can travel further than one phone's range, every device running Hops re-sends any emergency flare, flare cancellation, or Lost & Found post it hears. Once each, for a few seconds. A phone standing between the sender and someone further away becomes a stepping stone — that's how an alert crosses a building instead of a room.

What that means for you:
• Your phone will pass on alerts from people you don't know
• Each one goes once, so it can't loop or flood you
• ONLY those broadcast alerts. Your private messages are never relayed through anyone else's phone
• It's always on while Hops is running. If you'd rather not take part, sign out or uninstall
• A phone without Hops never relays anything

📄 WHAT HOPS KEEPS, in one breath.

On the server: your username, your email address (encrypted), a scrambled version of your password, and a key that lets emergency alerts be proved genuine. Plus any moderation record about your account, and Community Alerts from your admins.

That's it. Your messages, contacts, tasks, study tags and files are never uploaded.

No GPS. Hops has no location-tracking code at all — Android asks for a location permission because it won't let any app scan for Bluetooth without one, not because Hops wants your position.

Your rights are in the app, not in a form: Export My Data, Edit Identity, Delete Account. Full Terms are on the sign-up screen and the privacy policy is on hopsapp.me.

👀 ENDING A WATCH — either side can, at any time.

In Watch Me you'll see two lists: people you're watching, and people watching you. Both have a stop button.

That matters: if someone is watching you and you'd rather they weren't, you don't have to ask them to stop. You end it from your side and their phone is told.

It's best-effort over Bluetooth, like everything else here — if the message misses, it's corrected the next time either of you does anything. Ask me about "watch me" for what the feature actually does.
